proposed_sequence.spoken: A rose has thorns ... no thorn grows inside your mind.
proposed_sequence.direction: Start on the real engraved thorn/stem, reveal the carmine corolla, then cut to the painted gaze. Let the exact painting texture replace generic line-art diagrams.

proposed_sequence.spoken: Knowing is not swallowing the object ... matter stays outside.
proposed_sequence.direction: A close view of Watteau’s open fingers alongside a separate solid botanical stem; keep both real source images distinguishable, with an elegant editorial wipe rather than fake plant transfer.

proposed_sequence.spoken: The living plant exists in the garden ... act of understanding.
proposed_sequence.direction: Travel through the painted outdoor garden, then make a clear cut into the reader’s interior and upturned face. No speculative historical identification.

proposed_sequence.spoken: Different modes of presence ... not two little plants.
proposed_sequence.direction: Keep the human subject and singular rose concrete; the visible artistic composition is an analogy, not an anatomical picture of a rose literally inside a head.

proposed_sequence.spoken: Understanding reaches the rose itself through a likeness.
proposed_sequence.direction: Relate painted eye direction to the unchanged flower, then return emphasis to the flower itself. Do not make the portrait blink or act.

proposed_sequence.spoken: Form of another thing without becoming that thing materially.
proposed_sequence.direction: Use the lower painted roses as a rich material conclusion, then resolve on the single carmine hero bloom; do not equate knowledge with an inner pictorial theatre.

limits: These are acquired historical artworks, not AI-generated scenes or moving-footage takes.
Suggested regions are editorial guidance in normalized source coordinates, not baked image edits.
An eye-band crop has fewer source pixels than the full portrait: avoid enlarging it across the entire full-resolution vertical frame.
The botanical plate has fine, naturally small thorns; use stem-and-leaf close views rather than implying microscopic thorn photography.
Main editor chooses final integration, motion and delivery. No composition, audio or thumbnail was edited in this acquisition task.
